Jonckheere-Terpstra Test for Ordered Alternatives

Source: R/jonckheereTerpstraTest.R
jonckheereTerpstraTest.Rd

Performs the Jonckheere-Terpstra test for ordered alternatives across \(k\) independent groups.

The test assesses whether observations tend to increase (or decrease) systematically with group order.

Exact p-values are computed whenever feasible and valid (small samples without ties). For larger samples or tied data, permutation or asymptotic approximations are used.

jonckheereTerpstraTest(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'formula'
jonckheereTerpstraTest(formula, data, subset, na.action, ...)

# Default S3 method
jonckheereTerpstraTest(
  x,
  g,
  alternative = c("increasing", "decreasing", "two.sided"),
  method = c("auto", "exact", "permutation", "asymptotic"),
  R = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of observations, or a list of numeric vectors.

...

Further arguments passed to methods.

formula

Formula interface of the form lhs ~ rhs.

data

Optional data frame for the formula interface.

subset

Optional subset expression.

na.action

NA handling function.

g

Grouping variable. Ignored if x is a list.

alternative

Character string specifying the alternative: "increasing", "decreasing", or "two.sided".

method

Character string specifying the inference method: "auto" (default), "exact", "permutation", or "asymptotic". "auto" uses exact inference when possible (no ties, \(n \le 100\)), otherwise asymptotic.

R

Number of permutations. Required when method = "permutation".

Value

An object of class "htest" containing:

  • statistic,

  • p-value,

  • method,

  • alternative,

  • sample size information.

Details

A nonparametric test for monotonic trends across ordered independent groups.

The Jonckheere-Terpstra statistic is:

$$ JT = \sum_{k<l} \sum_{ij} \left[ I(X_{ik} < X_{jl}) + \frac12 I(X_{ik} = X_{jl}) \right] $$

where \(i,j\) index observations from ordered groups \(k,l\).

Large values of the statistic indicate increasing trends across groups.

Exact inference

Exact p-values are computed from the exact permutation distribution using a dynamic programming recursion implemented in C++.

Exact inference is only available:

  • without ties,

  • for total sample sizes \(n \le 100\).

Permutation inference

When ties are present or sample sizes are large, permutation p-values can be computed by permuting group labels under the null hypothesis. The number of permutations is controlled by R.

This approach remains valid in the presence of ties.

Asymptotic approximation

If method = "asymptotic" or no other method applies, a normal approximation with tie-corrected variance is applied.

References

Jonckheere, A. R. (1954). A distribution-free k-sample test against ordered alternatives. Biometrika, 41, 133–145.

Terpstra, T. J. (1952). The asymptotic normality and consistency of Kendall's test against trend. Indagationes Mathematicae, 14, 327–333.

See also

Other test.trend: cochranArmitageTest(), mantelTrendTest(), pageTest()

Examples


set.seed(1)

g <- ordered(rep(1:4, each = 10))

x <- rnorm(40) + 0.5 * as.numeric(g)

jonckheereTerpstraTest(x, g)
#> 
#> 	Jonckheere-Terpstra Test for Ordered Alternatives (exact)
#> 
#> data:  x and g
#> JT = 437, k = 4, n = 40, p-value = 0.0003781
#> alternative hypothesis: increasing
#> 

x[1:2] <- mean(x[1:2])

jonckheereTerpstraTest(x, g, method = "permutation", R = 2000)
#> 
#> 	Jonckheere-Terpstra Test for Ordered Alternatives (permutation, R =
#> 	2000)
#> 
#> data:  x and g
#> JT = 438, k = 4, n = 40, p-value < 2.2e-16
#> alternative hypothesis: increasing
#> 

coffee <- list(
  c_4 = c(447,396,383,410),
  c_2 = c(438,521,468,391,504,472),
  c_0 = c(513,543,506,489,407)
)

jonckheereTerpstraTest(coffee)
#> 
#> 	Jonckheere-Terpstra Test for Ordered Alternatives (exact)
#> 
#> data:  x
#> JT = 59, k = 3, n = 15, p-value = 0.009866
#> alternative hypothesis: increasing
#> 

# Hollander-Wolfe-Chicken Example 6.2 
#   Motivational Effect of Knowledge of Performance

motiv <- list(
  no    = c(40,35,38,43,44,41),
  rough = c(38,40,47,44,40,42),
  acc   = c(48,40,45,43,46,44))

jonckheereTerpstraTest(motiv, method = "auto")    # here: exact
#> 
#> 	Jonckheere-Terpstra Test for Ordered Alternatives (asymptotic)
#> 
#> data:  x
#> JT = 79, k = 3, n = 18, p-value = 0.02071
#> alternative hypothesis: increasing
#> 
jonckheereTerpstraTest(motiv, method = "exact")   # exact:       p ~ 0.038
#> Warning: exact inference not available with ties; falling back to asymptotic approximation
#> 
#> 	Jonckheere-Terpstra Test for Ordered Alternatives (asymptotic)
#> 
#> data:  x
#> JT = 79, k = 3, n = 18, p-value = 0.02071
#> alternative hypothesis: increasing
#> 
jonckheereTerpstraTest(motiv, method = "asymp")   # asymptotic:  p ~ 0.032
#> 
#> 	Jonckheere-Terpstra Test for Ordered Alternatives (asymptotic)
#> 
#> data:  x
#> JT = 79, k = 3, n = 18, p-value = 0.02071
#> alternative hypothesis: increasing
#> 

set.seed(42)
jonckheereTerpstraTest(motiv, method = "perm", R= 10000)   # permutation: p ~ 0.038
#> 
#> 	Jonckheere-Terpstra Test for Ordered Alternatives (permutation, R =
#> 	10000)
#> 
#> data:  x
#> JT = 79, k = 3, n = 18, p-value = 0.0193
#> alternative hypothesis: increasing
#>
